video_title: Kenrich Williams on Team's Mindset | Postgame Media | November 23, 2026

quotes.speaker: Kenrich Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams on the importance of competing in every game
quotes.excerpt: It's easy to make excuses in this league, but as long as you compete, you give yourself a chance.
quotes.quote: I think we came out and competed. That's the main battle, is competing, not laying down. It's easy to make excuses in this league, but as long as you compete, you give yourself a chance every night. I'm proud of the guys, the effort that we showed. We came up short, but there's things to build off of.
quotes.social_post: Kenrich Williams says the main battle for the Thunder is simply competing and not laying down despite the recent loss. He believes the effort is there to build on.

structured.context: Kenrich Williams discusses the team's effort and mindset following a postgame loss.

quotes.speaker: Kenrich Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams on adjusting to a roster with many new players
quotes.excerpt: The principles don't change throughout the years, it's been the same, but it's going to be an adjustment.
quotes.quote: It's an adjustment. The principles don't change throughout the years, it's been the same, but it's going to be an adjustment. Playing with new guys and the younger guys having to step up early and learn the system. With reps, you gain confidence on that side of the ball, so we'll be better. It's only November, so we still got a lot of room for growth and we'll be better.
quotes.social_post: Kenrich Williams on the Thunder adjusting to a new roster. He notes that while the principles remain the same, it takes time for younger players to learn the system and gain confidence.

structured.context: Kenrich Williams talks about the adjustment period for the team's younger players learning the system.

quotes.speaker: Kenrich Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams on taking the season one game at a time
quotes.excerpt: Taking it one game at a time, keeping our heads where we're at right now.
quotes.quote: Taking it one game at a time, keeping our heads where we're at right now, where our feet are. It'll come along. I'm not worried about that. I've been on both sides, so there's room for growth. We can get better as a team and everybody, including myself. We take these steps and just keep chipping away.
quotes.social_post: Kenrich Williams says the team is focused on taking it one game at a time and keeping their heads where their feet are as they look for growth.

structured.context: Kenrich Williams reflects on the team's approach to the long NBA season.

quotes.speaker: Kenrich Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams on learning from close game situations
quotes.excerpt: In the long run, it pays off because you've been in these situations.
quotes.quote: You look at these games and you're like, man, we keep coming up short, but in the long run, it pays off because you've been in these situations. A couple plays away, so you just take a step back and say, how can we be better and what are we learning from every game situation? I'm grateful to be in this position.
quotes.social_post: Kenrich Williams believes the experience of losing close games will pay off for the Thunder in the long run as they learn from every situation.

structured.context: Kenrich Williams discusses the value of learning from close game losses.

quotes.speaker: Kenrich Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams on Jalen Williams' competitive nature
quotes.excerpt: He is one of the most competitive guys that I've ever been around.
quotes.quote: He is one of the most competitive guys that I've ever been around. Not just the game of basketball, it's just everyday, how he attacks the day. He always just shows up for a moment and is super competitive.
quotes.social_post: Kenrich Williams calls Jalen Williams one of the most competitive guys he has ever been around. He says Jalen attacks every single day with that same intensity.

structured.context: Kenrich Williams praises the competitive nature of his teammate Jalen Williams.

quotes.speaker: Kenrich Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams on the challenges of playing with different teammates
quotes.excerpt: You got to learn and adapt to new guys and their playstyle.
quotes.quote: I would say just learning how guys want the ball and tendencies. Coming into the season, you pretty much knew who was going to play night in and night out, and things change like that. You got to learn and adapt to new guys and their playstyle. It takes longer than a month, so it's something that myself and all the other guys, even on the flip side, the younger guys having to adjust to the way I play or the way Jalen plays.
quotes.social_post: Kenrich Williams discusses the challenge of learning teammate tendencies. He says it takes longer than a month to adjust to how different guys want the ball and their specific playstyles.

structured.context: Kenrich Williams explains the difficulty of adapting to new teammates and their specific playstyles.

quotes.speaker: Kenrich Williams
quotes.summary_phrase: Kenrich Williams on his experience playing the five position
quotes.excerpt: Just battling, doing whatever the team needs me to do.
quotes.quote: Just battling, doing whatever the team needs me to do, whether that's playing a five or playing any position on the court. I just try to show up for my team and give my best effort. I definitely look back on those times where I played the five and you just try to figure out what the team needs at that time, at that position, and just try to go attack.
quotes.social_post: Kenrich Williams on playing the five position for the Thunder. He says he is just focused on battling and doing whatever the team needs him to do to give his best effort.

structured.context: Kenrich Williams discusses his willingness to play different positions, including the five, to help the team.
